comments.body:
DIAGNOSIS — the premise as filed is FALSE, and the fleet-wide unblock needs NO code change. Evidence below; I have not claimed this ticket because the recorded direction (extract a seam from close_ticket) would be wrong.

MAIN IS GREEN. On current main tip 07e76a1ce3: ruff reports close_ticket at complexity 17, and .github/complexity-baseline.json records ceiling 17. Consistent. `check_complexity_baseline.py --check` on a clean main checkout returns: active=60 new=0 increased=0 stale=0. At the sha in the report, 104dc4e10a, code was 19 and the recorded ceiling was ALSO 19 — likewise consistent. Neither sha has a 19-vs-17 mismatch in its own tree, so there is nothing in close_ticket to extract.

WHAT ACTUALLY FAILS. The CI job runs --lock, not --check. lock_against_base (scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:455+) compares the CHANGE's baseline against MAIN TIP's, and its rules are: an entry REMOVED or a ceiling LOWERED is allowed; a ceiling RAISED or a NEW entry is a violation requiring an administrator.

My damselfly change (merged as 8f6b6c9356) extracted the signing tail from close_ticket, taking it 19 -> 17, and drained the now-stale baseline entry 19 -> 17. Lowering a ceiling is explicitly allowed, so that change passed. But it means every OPEN change whose tree still carries the pre-damselfly baseline presents ceiling 19 against main's 17 — which the lock reads as RAISING the ceiling.

REPRODUCED EXACTLY. Feeding main-tip ceilings as base and the 104dc4e10a ceilings as branch into lock_against_base returns exactly one violation:

  ceiling RAISED for 'src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py::close_ticket': 17 -> 19 — an administrator must override the gate to raise a ceiling

That is the reported symptom, verbatim. The same call with a rebased branch (base vs base) returns ZERO violations.

IMMEDIATE UNBLOCK, NO ADMIN NEEDED: every blocked change REBASES onto current main. It does not need a new patchset beyond the rebase, and it does not need an administrator override. Any change that has not rebased since 8f6b6c9356 landed is affected; a change that never touches the baseline still carries the old FILE and so still trips it.

THE REAL DEFECT, if this ticket is kept. The lock compares against main TIP rather than the change's MERGE BASE, so it cannot distinguish 'this branch raised a ceiling' from 'main lowered it underneath an un-rebased branch'. Any future ceiling REDUCTION on main will re-break the fleet the same way — and reductions are exactly what the shrink-only ratchet is designed to encourage, so the gate currently penalises the behaviour it exists to reward. A durable fix compares the branch against merge-base(main, branch) and flags only entries the branch itself changed. Note the CI lock fetches main with --depth=1 (scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:_fetch_base_ceilings_from_main), which is too shallow to compute a merge base, so that fetch depth has to change too.

I have NOT claimed this ticket: its recorded direction is based on the false premise, and the re-scoped work (a CI-gate correctness fix) is a different change from the one described. Awaiting a decision on whether to proceed with the merge-base fix under this ticket or a new one.

comments.body:
Implemented as change https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1682 (commit 9a41f5d9f3).

PREMISE: the ticket as FILED was refuted (main is green; close_ticket is 17 against a ceiling of 17 on tip, and was 19 against 19 at the reported sha). Rescoped in place to the real defect, per the grayling/wolverine precedent. Full diagnosis and the verbatim reproduction are in the earlier comment and the description.

CHANGE. _base_commit_for_comparison(main_ref) returns merge-base(main, HEAD) and the lock is judged against the baseline AT that commit, so only entries the BRANCH itself changed can violate. lock_against_base's rules are untouched — only the base handed to it changes. The fetch drops --depth=1 (too shallow to compute a merge base) and unshallows a shallow checkout before trying.

FALLBACK DIRECTION IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART. When no merge base can be computed the gate falls back to the previous main-tip comparison and prints that it did. Tip comparison is STRICTER — it can only over-report — so an unavailable merge base can never let a genuine ceiling raise through. Fail-closed posture preserved; the fallback degrades toward noise, never toward permissiveness.

EVIDENCE. 6 new tests, 78 passing in tests/unit/test_complexity_baseline.py (72 before). They run against a REAL two-branch git repo built in a fixture — main lowers a ceiling after a branch forked and the branch never touches the baseline — rather than mocked ceilings, so the scenario is the incident's actual shape.

The regression test carries its own INVERSE proof: after asserting the un-rebased branch now passes against the merge base, it asserts that the same branch ceilings against main's TIP still produce a violation. So the test would pass trivially if the fix were reverted only in one direction; it pins both halves.

Also covered: a genuine raise relative to the fork point still fails; a NEW entry still fails; a branch that lowers or removes still passes; and unrelated histories (orphan branch, no merge base) fall back to the tip and say so.

make lint (incl. the complexity baseline gate itself) and make typecheck (513 files) clean.

OPERATIONAL NOTE for anyone still blocked before this lands: rebasing onto current main clears it today, with no admin override.

compiled_state.description:
## Refuted premise (as originally filed)

Filed as: current `origin/main` fails the locked complexity gate because `close_ticket` in
`transition_close.py` reports 19 against a recorded ceiling of 17, to be fixed by extracting
along a seam.

**That is false, and the suggested remedy would have changed working code without unblocking
anyone.** Verified:

* main tip `07e76a1ce3`: ruff reports `close_ticket` at **17**, and
  `.github/complexity-baseline.json` records **17**. `--check` on a clean checkout returns
  `active=60 new=0 increased=0 stale=0`.
* the sha in the report, `104dc4e10a`: code **19**, recorded ceiling **19**.

Neither tree contains a 19-vs-17 mismatch. There is nothing in `close_ticket` to extract.

## The real defect

CI runs `--lock`, not `--check`. `lock_against_base`
(`scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:455`) compares the CHANGE's baseline against **main
TIP**: a REMOVED entry or a LOWERED ceiling is allowed; a RAISED ceiling or a NEW entry is a
violation needing an administrator.

Change 1673 (merged `8f6b6c9356`) extracted the signing tail from `close_ticket`, taking it
19 -> 17, and drained the stale baseline entry 19 -> 17. Lowering is allowed, so it passed.
But every OPEN change whose tree still carries the pre-1673 baseline now presents ceiling 19
against main's 17 — which the lock reads as RAISING it.

**Verbatim reproduction.** Feeding main-tip ceilings as `base` and `104dc4e10a`'s as `branch`
into `lock_against_base` returns exactly one violation:

```
ceiling RAISED for 'src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py::close_ticket': 17 -> 19 —
an administrator must override the gate to raise a ceiling
```

That is the reported symptom, verbatim. The same call with a rebased branch returns ZERO.

So the gate cannot distinguish "this branch RAISED a ceiling" from "main LOWERED it underneath
an un-rebased branch". It blames the branch for a change main made. This is not specific to
1673: **every future ceiling reduction on main will break the fleet identically**, so the
shrink-only ratchet currently punishes the shrinking it exists to reward. A change that never
touches the baseline is still hit, because it still carries the old FILE.

Immediate operational unblock (no code, no admin): affected changes REBASE onto current main.

## Direction

Compare the branch against **`merge-base(main, HEAD)`** rather than main tip, so only entries
the BRANCH itself changed can violate.

* `_fetch_base_ceilings_from_main` (`:494`) currently fetches `--depth=1`, which is too
  shallow to compute a merge base. Fetch main with enough history, and if the local checkout
  is shallow (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`) deepen it before retrying.
* Read the baseline at the merge-base commit and use it as `base`. `lock_against_base`'s rules
  are unchanged — only the base it is given changes.
* **Fallback direction matters.** If a merge base still cannot be computed, fall back to
  today's main-tip comparison with an explicit note. That fallback is STRICTER, never looser:
  it can only over-report, so an unavailable merge base can never let a genuine ceiling raise
  through. Fail-closed posture is preserved.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An un-rebased branch carrying the pre-reduction baseline PASSES the lock after main
      lowers a ceiling — verified by a test reproducing exactly that scenario
- [ ] A branch that genuinely RAISES a ceiling relative to its merge base still FAILS —
      verified by a test
- [ ] A branch that adds a NEW entry still FAILS — verified by a test
- [ ] A ceiling LOWERED or an entry REMOVED by the branch still passes — verified by a test
- [ ] When no merge base can be computed the gate falls back to the main-tip comparison and
      says so, never silently passing a genuine raise — verified by a test

regression tests for the lowered-ceiling scenario and the genuine-raise/new-entry cases
